title: The Stickball Scoreboard
tagline: A 1920s New York stickball game in Three.js, built by a swarm of agents and judged against Backyard Baseball by fresh critics who look only at rendered frames. Paused after the stage conversion: 45 scenarios render clean, nine critiques are in, and no piece has yet been signed off.

pieces.name: Backyard Baseball dossier
pieces.what: The quality bar, written down as checkable specifics critics can score a screenshot against.
pieces.gap: Proxy blocked image access, so colour numbers are derived from the design language rather than measured off real frames.

pieces.name: 1925 New York dossier
pieces.what: Tenement anatomy, street furniture, stickball's real rules and slang, with dimensions.
pieces.gap: Kid dialogue is reconstructed from 1940s-60s sources; 1925 transcripts were unreachable.

pieces.name: Design bible
pieces.what: Resolves bright-Backyard against sooty-1925: palette, shading, comedy register, 12 signature moments.
pieces.gap: Amended twice mid-build: section 17 (the 2D stage model) and 17.6 (staged scale).

pieces.name: Street architecture
pieces.what: Tenement facades, stoops, fire escapes, cornices, water towers, storefronts, the El.
pieces.gap: Built and re-staged onto backdrop cards. Never judged — its critics all died in the API outage.

pieces.name: Surface & props
pieces.what: Belgian block, chalk bases, manhole home plate, hydrant, ash cans, pushcart, Model T, laundry lines.

pieces.name: Sky, light & air
pieces.what: Late-afternoon canyon light, coal haze, smoke, pigeons, wind, time of day.
pieces.gap: Sky, atmosphere and the light rig landed; the builder died mid-round. Never judged.

pieces.name: Art direction & shading
pieces.what: The toon/painted look, outlines, colour grade — how sooty becomes cheerful.
pieces.gap: Palette with real colour arithmetic, materials and postfx landed. Never judged.

pieces.name: Character art
pieces.what: Proportions, faces, expressions, period wardrobe, silhouettes you can tell apart at a glance.
pieces.gap: Sixteen parametric kids with faces and period wardrobe. Never judged.

pieces.name: Animation vocabulary
pieces.what: Idles, windups, swings, run cycles, slides, dives, catches, celebrations, taunts.
pieces.gap: Clip system, fidgets and state machine landed after 20 self-critique passes. Never judged.

pieces.name: Roster & personality
pieces.what: Sixteen neighbourhood kids with stats, attitudes, catchphrases and a team-select screen.
pieces.gap: Sixteen kids, cigarette-card portraits, choosin-up-sides screen. The strongest piece in the build. Never judged.

pieces.name: Stage camera
pieces.what: Long lens, two locked framings, cuts instead of camera moves.
pieces.gap: Round 3 critic: 4.0. The two framings still read as one shot; staged scale (17.6) arrived too late for it to use.

pieces.name: Backdrop layers
pieces.what: The canyon rebuilt as five flat scenery cards with parallax.
pieces.gap: Round 2 critic: 4.2. Five flat cards built; the far half of the set is the least authored thing in frame.

pieces.name: Field layout
pieces.what: Every position on a shallow stage, as one source of truth.
pieces.gap: Round 1 critic: 4.4. layout.js is now the single source of truth; the catcher sits off the pitch axis in the main framing.

pieces.name: Pitching
pieces.what: Aim, windup, pitch types, the junk a 12-year-old throws, pitcher AI.
pieces.gap: Pitch set, windup theatre, pitcher AI. Never judged.

pieces.name: Batting & contact
pieces.what: Timing, aim, swing types, the contact model, hitstop and weight.

pieces.name: Ball physics & caroms
pieces.what: Spaldeen bounce, wall and fire-escape caroms, stoop ricochets, windows, the sewer shot.
pieces.gap: Spaldeen flight, swept-sphere caroms, per-surface behaviour. Never judged.

pieces.name: Fielding
pieces.what: Chase, catch, dive, relay, throws, errors, kids who are bad at it on purpose.

pieces.name: Baserunning
pieces.what: Runners, tag-ups, steals, slides into a chalk base, close plays.

pieces.name: Street rules & game flow
pieces.what: Two sewers, ghost runners, do-overs, CAR!, innings, the shape of a whole game.

pieces.name: Camera direction
pieces.what: Cuts, follows, replays, slow-mo, the home-run camera.

pieces.name: Scorebug & HUD
pieces.what: Period lettering, count, bases, outs — readable in one glance.

pieces.name: Menus & screens
pieces.what: Title, team select, pause, between-innings cards, results.

pieces.name: Juice
pieces.what: Dust, impact stars, comic lettering, trails, confetti, shake, hitstop.

pieces.name: 1920s score
pieces.what: Procedural ragtime and hot jazz that ducks under the action.
pieces.gap: Round 2 critic: 7.1. Score is written and provably swings; the title theme still never sounds against a suspended AudioContext.

pieces.name: City & game sound
pieces.what: Crack of the broom handle, footsteps, traffic, the El, a dog, a window.
pieces.gap: Round 2 critic: 8.2, the highest score in the build. Blocked on aliveness and feel — 823 WebAudio nodes rebuilt every 7 seconds.

pieces.name: Announcer & kid chatter
pieces.what: Play-by-play with cadence, taunts, speech bubbles, running gags.
pieces.gap: Round 1 critic: 6.4. Writing is strong; the escalation timing never reaches the screen.

pieces.name: Controls & onboarding
pieces.what: Keyboard, mouse, touch, gamepad, and a first minute that teaches itself.

pieces.name: Performance
pieces.what: Draw calls, instancing, LOD — 60fps with the whole block alive.

pieces.name: Signature moments
pieces.what: The twelve beats a player would tell a friend about, each actually producible.

pieces.name: Cohesion pass
pieces.what: One agent plays the whole game and smooths it into a single coherent thing.

wire.text: Stopped at the users request. 45 scenarios render with zero console errors; the single-file build is 1.4MB. Nine critic verdicts in, all NOT_YET. Highest score: the sound engine at 8.2.
Switched from a 3D street canyon to 3D characters on a 2D stage. Stage conformance went from 166 violations across 30 scenarios to 37 across 45, and 25 scenarios are now fully legal.

Twice the conformance tool encoded a bad assumption — a builder bought the height floor by collapsing the lens to 9.8 degrees, and the long lens flattened the size hierarchy that tells you who a shot is about. The critics caught both, because they look at frames.
Nine pieces have never been judged at all — their critics died in the API outage. Four gameplay pieces, the whole picture layer and all of the polish wave remain unbuilt.
